title: Exercise 7A · Q8
summary: The height meets UV at its midpoint H, giving a right-angled ΔTUH.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q8: The figure shows an isosceles triangle TUV where TU = TV = 9.6 m and UV = 15.4 m. Find the height, TH, of the triangle.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: The figure shows an **isosceles triangle TUV** where **TU = TV = 9.6 m** and **UV = 15.4 m**. We have to find the height **TH**.

steps.title: H is the midpoint of UV
steps.narration: In an isosceles triangle the height from the apex meets the base at its **midpoint**. So **UH is half of UV**.\[\begin{aligned}UH &= \frac{15.4}{2} \\ &= 7.7\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔTUH, **∠H = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **TU**. The other two sides meet at the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{UH^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Make the unknown the subject
steps.narration: We want a **shorter side**, so subtract the known square from the hypotenuse square.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{UH^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TU^2} - \role{legA}{UH^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{UH^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TU^2} - \role{legA}{UH^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{9.6^2} - \role{legA}{7.7^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 32.87 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{UH^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TU^2} - \role{legA}{UH^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{9.6^2} - \role{legA}{7.7^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{92.16} - \role{legA}{59.29} \\ &= \role{legB}{32.87} \\ \role{legB}{TH} &= \sqrt{32.87} = \role{ans}{5.73\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check UH
challenges.prompt: UV = 15.4 m and H is the midpoint. How long is **UH**?

takeaways: The height of an **isosceles** triangle meets the base at its **midpoint**, creating two right-angled triangles.
Use one of those right-angled triangles with Pythagoras' theorem.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
